newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: EON SHARES TUMBLE ON MIX OF RUMOURS.
newsitem.headline: EON SHARES TUMBLE ON MIX OF RUMOURS.

text.p: Shares of national car distributor Edaran Otomobil Nasional Bhd (EON) tumbled on worries over its future earnings, analysts and dealers said.
At 0810 GMT, EON shares were down 1.70 ringgit or 9.24 percent to 16.70 on volume of 346,000 shares traded.

There was market talk that the company would be hit by slower earnings growth projected by carmaker Perusahaan Otmobil Nasional Bhd, the possible sale of EON's banking unit and the taking away of its car-distribution rights.
EON distributes the popular Proton cars made by Proton Bhd.
But some dealers said the stock was merely falling on extension of sell orders of Malaysian blue-chip shares.
Officials at EON, Proton and their parent company, the DRB-Hicom group were not immediately available for comment.

"EON is probably down on the ringgit (weakness), and (Proton chairman) Saleh (Sulong)'s comments yesterday about slower earnings growth at Proton next year," said Tony Shue, vice-president of institutional sales at Jupiter Securities.
Saleh told reporters on Thursday: "We (Proton) may not be able to register the same growth rate (in 1998)."

Some analysts said there was a possibility that under a restructuring plan, EON may be hiving off its banking unit, EON Bank. Such a move would take away about 20 percent of its net profit, said an automotive analyst at a foreign brokerage.
"People are worried about what's to fill the void in earnings if this comes about," the analyst said. But she said there was no confirmation on the speculation.
There was also talk that DRB-Hicom may pass distribution rights of Proton cars to Usahasama Proton-DRB (USPD), a member of DRB-Hicom, under a restructuring plan.
Another analyst said EON's margins may be hit by the recent surge in interest rates. Apart from EON Bank, EON has two finance houses under its arms.

"EON is weak because of its banking exposure. The increasing interest rates mean that their cost of borrowing is going up, while their lending is fixed," said Soh Meng Hui, research manager at KL City Securities.
